docs.text:
decode_class_a_prefix(counts: dict[str, int], n: int, q: int, layout: dict[str, list[int] | int], total_qubits: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Decode the prefix-stage output: (num_signed, den_unsigned) per pixel.

The register width is taken from layout, so the same decoder serves every G.

Returns:

Type Description (num_image, den_image)

Both 2^n x 2^n int arrays. num_image is the signed two's-complement value of the num register, i.e. 2^f I_a - K I_b (I_a - I_b for G_eff = 1). den_image is the unsigned 2^f I_a + K I_b. The GP is num_image / den_image where den_image > 0.

docs.title: affine_subtract_constant
docs.text:
affine_subtract_constant(qc: QuantumCircuit, R_qubits: list[int], c_value: int, output_signed_qubits: list[int], c_const_register_qubits: list[int], sub_carry_qubits: list[int]) -> None

Compute output_signed = R - c_value (signed two's-complement, width q + 1) where c_value is a classical non-negative integer and R is a q-bit unsigned quantum register.

The trick is to materialise the classical constant c_value into an ancilla register via X gates, run the standard ripple-carry subtractor, then X-unset the ancilla. The ancilla returns to |0⟩ on exit (provided it was |0⟩ on entry).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default R_qubits list[int]

q-bit unsigned input register, preserved on exit.

required c_value int

Classical non-negative integer in [0, 2^(q+1) - 1].

required output_signed_qubits list[int]

q + 1-bit register, |0⟩ on entry; holds (R - c_value) mod 2^(q+1) on exit (MSB is the sign bit).

required c_const_register_qubits list[int]

q + 1-bit ancilla, |0⟩ on entry and exit. Used to hold c_value temporarily during the subtract.

required sub_carry_qubits list[int]

q + 2-bit carry register for the subtractor, |0⟩ on entry, dirty on exit (carries from the subtract).

required Notes

Cost: 2 · popcount(c_value) X gates + one q_sub of width q + 1 ≈ 4 (q + 1) Toffolis.

This is the building block for the roGFP affine reparametrisation R_C = (R - R_red) / (R_ox - R_red). The division by the classical constant R_ox - R_red is naturally implemented downstream as a q_mul_const with k = 2^k_frac / (R_ox - R_red) in fixed point; :func:class_c_rogfp_full packages the full composition.

Composition example (Class B → affine subtract, autonomous Class C without the optional 1/(R_ox - R_red) rescaling)::

from qiskit import QuantumRegister
from qimp.processing.ratiometric_circuit import (
    class_b_ratio, affine_subtract_constant,
)

# Stage 1: build Class B (autonomous integer ratio R = I_a // I_b).
qc, layout = class_b_ratio(image_a, image_b, q=2)

# Stage 2: append Class C registers and apply affine subtract.
start = qc.num_qubits
q_w = q + 1
R_C_reg = QuantumRegister(q_w, "R_C_signed")
R_red_reg = QuantumRegister(q_w, "R_red_const")
sub_c_reg = QuantumRegister(q_w + 1, "sub_carry_C")
qc.add_register(R_C_reg, R_red_reg, sub_c_reg)

R_C_idx     = list(range(start,             start + q_w))
R_red_idx   = list(range(start + q_w,       start + 2 * q_w))
sub_c_idx   = list(range(start + 2 * q_w,   start + 2 * q_w + q_w + 1))

affine_subtract_constant(
    qc,
    R_qubits=layout["quotient"],   # = R from Class B
    c_value=R_red,
    output_signed_qubits=R_C_idx,
    c_const_register_qubits=R_red_idx,
    sub_carry_qubits=sub_c_idx,
)

# `R_C_idx` now holds (R - R_red) signed two's-complement.
# The classical decoder recovers R_C(p) = signed_value(p) / (R_ox - R_red).

For an in-circuit /(R_ox - R_red) rescaling, append a q_mul_const with k_bits encoding 2^k_frac / (R_ox - R_red) as a fixed-point integer; the multiply consumes R_C_idx as its b argument and writes the scaled result to a fresh accumulator.

At n=1, q=2 the whole pipeline needs about 35 qubits. Each primitive (q_div_restoring, affine_subtract_constant) has bit-exact unit tests, and :func:class_c_rogfp_full packages the composition.

docs.title: class_a_gp_full
docs.text:
class_a_gp_full(image_a: ndarray, image_b: ndarray, q: int, q_frac: int = 2, G: float = 1.0, g_frac_bits: int | None = None) -> tuple[QuantumCircuit, dict[str, list[int] | int]]

Full autonomous Class A GP circuit, GP = (I_a - G I_b) / (I_a + G I_b).

With G_eff = K / 2^f from :func:gp_g_fixed_point, A = 2^f I_a and B = K I_b (A = I_a, B = I_b for G_eff = 1), the circuit computes for each pixel in superposition:

magnitude(p) = floor(|A(p) - B(p)| * 2^q_frac / (A(p) + B(p)))
sign(p)      = 1  iff  B(p) > A(p)

The decoder reconstructs gp(p) = (-1)^sign(p) * magnitude(p) / 2^q_frac, which is the GP for G_eff truncated towards zero to q_frac fractional bits.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default image_a ndarray

As in :func:class_a_gp_prefix.

required image_b ndarray

As in :func:class_a_gp_prefix.

required q ndarray

As in :func:class_a_gp_prefix.

required q_frac int

Fractional bits of the output magnitude, >= 0.

2 G float

GP G-factor and its fixed-point representation, see :func:gp_g_fixed_point. The default G = 1.0 gives the plain normalised difference.

1.0 g_frac_bits float

GP G-factor and its fixed-point representation, see :func:gp_g_fixed_point. The default G = 1.0 gives the plain normalised difference.

1.0

Returns:

Type Description (qc, layout)

layout has keys position, I_a, I_b, num, den, add_c, sub_c, sign, ones_reg, inc_carry, num_scaled, quotient, div_work, div_pad, div_c, div_flag, and for G_eff != 1 also g_b, mul_c, mul_guard.

Notes

Pipeline (composition of tested primitives):

  1. dual_neqr_load(I_a, I_b).
  2. Only for G_eff != 1: g_b <- K * I_b via q_mul_const.
  3. den <- A + B and num <- A - B (w = L + 1 bits, num in two's complement), as in :func:class_a_gp_prefix.
  4. Copy num's MSB into a dedicated sign qubit.
  5. Conditional two's-complement negate of num: flip all bits (CNOT(sign, num[i])) then conditional +1 via q_add_ctrl against a 1-valued constant register, so num holds |A - B|.
  6. Bit-shift num up by q_frac into num_scaled (width w + q_frac).
  7. q_div_general(num_scaled, den): quotient holds the fractional GP magnitude.

Resources: with w = L + 1 (L = q for G_eff = 1, else max(q + f, q + bit_length(K))) and d = w + q_frac the circuit has 2n + 2q + 7w + 4 + 2d + (d + 1)(w + 2) qubits, plus L + popcount(K)(q + 2) + 1 for the multiplier when G_eff != 1. At n = 1, q = 2, q_frac = 2, G = 1 this is 71 qubits, past statevector range; use AerSimulator(method='matrix_product_state').

docs.title: decode_class_a_full
docs.text:
decode_class_a_full(counts: dict[str, int], n: int, q: int, q_frac: int, layout: dict[str, list[int] | int], total_qubits: int) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]

Decode Class A full counts into (gp_signed_image, divzero_mask).

Serves :func:class_a_gp_full and :func:class_a_gp_lookup for any G (the G factor only changes the circuit, not the read-out). Reads the sign qubit, the full quotient register, and the div_flag. The magnitude must be read across the whole register, not just its low q_frac bits: since |A - B| <= A + B the quotient is bounded by 2**q_frac, and it attains that value at the saturating GP = +-1 endpoints (one channel quantised to 0), which sets bit q_frac and would be truncated away by a low-bits read. Bits above q_frac are identically zero, so the full read is exact at every pixel.

Returns:

Type Description (gp_image, divzero_mask)

gp_image[r, c] = (-1)^sign * magnitude / 2^q_frac, floating-point in [-1, 1]. divzero_mask[r, c] is True for pixels where the denominator was 0 (I_a = I_b = 0, since G > 0).

docs.title: class_c_rogfp_full
docs.text:
class_c_rogfp_full(image_a: ndarray, image_b: ndarray, q: int, q_frac: int, R_red_fp: int) -> tuple[QuantumCircuit, dict[str, list[int] | int]]

Full autonomous Class C roGFP calibrated-ratio circuit.

For each pixel in superposition the circuit computes, entirely on the quantum device, the fixed-point quantities

ratio(p)    = floor(I_a(p) * 2^q_frac / I_b(p))      (fractional R)
rc_signed(p)= ratio(p) - R_red_fp                    (signed)

where R_red_fp = round(R_red * 2^q_frac) is the classical reduced reference in fixed point. The classical decoder finishes the affine reparametrisation with the single classical calibration scalar

R_C(p) = rc_signed(p) / ((R_ox - R_red) * 2^q_frac)  in [0, 1]

This is how a wet-lab roGFP calibration applies (R_ox - R_red), and it parallels the /2^q_frac scalar of the Class-A decoder. The fractional ratio (shift by q_frac then non-square divide) is what lifts the integer-quotient degeneracy that makes Class B uninformative for roGFP at small q (the sub-unit physiological F405/F488 ratio).

Pipeline (composition of already-tested primitives): 1. dual_neqr_load(I_a, I_b) 2. Bit-shift I_a up by q_frac into num_scaled (CNOT copy). 3. q_div_general(num_scaled, I_b) → ratio holds the fixed-point fractional ratio; the div-zero flag is set iff I_b == 0. 4. affine_subtract_constant(ratio, R_red_fp) → rc_signed holds ratio - R_red_fp (signed two's-complement).

Resource budget at n=1, q=4, q_frac=4: about 114 qubits, beyond laptop statevector simulation. Use AerSimulator(method='matrix_product_state'): the bond dimension stays small because the position register superposes only 4^n pixel branches.

docs.title: apply_gp_function
docs.text:
apply_gp_function(qc: QuantumCircuit, n: int, m: int, params: Sequence[Parameter | float]) -> QuantumCircuit

Append the parameterised GP sub-circuit in place (per-pixel).

For each of the 2^(2n) pixel positions, two parameters drive:

  1. a fully-controlled RY on the green branch (position matches + selection qubit = 1) writing onto the color qubit (the "G half"),
  2. a fully-controlled RY on the red branch (position matches + selection qubit = 0) writing onto the same color qubit (the "R half"), followed by an unconditional Hadamard that interferes the two channel amplitudes.

Splitting the two rotations across the two selection branches is what makes the per-pixel parameter pair non-degenerate: had both rotations sat on the same selection branch, they would compose into a single RY(θ₁+θ₂) and the model would have only one effective parameter per pixel. (Older versions of this function also missed the position-matching controls — the X-flip mask was applied but the CRY took only selection_qubit as control, so every pixel branch produced the same rotation. Both bugs are fixed.)

The circuit assumes the standard FRQI layout: n row qubits, n column qubits, m selection qubits, 1 color qubit (color qubit index = 2n+m).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default qc QuantumCircuit

Circuit to modify. Must already encode the FRQI representation of two channels (so it has 2n+m+1 qubits).

required n int

Spatial qubits per axis (so image size = 2^n × 2^n).

required m int

Image-selection qubits (so number of stacked images = 2^m). Must be ≥ 1 for the GP construction (we need a selection qubit to be the extra control).

required params Sequence[Parameter | float]

Sequence of 2 · 2^(2n) parameters. Built externally via [Parameter(f"θ{i}") for i in range(2 * 2**(2*n))] and assigned later with qc.assign_parameters(...).

required

Type Description QuantumCircuit

The same qc, mutated in place and returned for chaining.

docs.text:
analytical_gp_params(green: ndarray, red: ndarray, *, alpha: float = 1.0, normalization: float | None = None, target: ndarray | None = None) -> np.ndarray

Return the closed-form optimal parameters for :func:apply_gp_function.

With the final Hadamard moved outside the per-pixel loop (see apply_gp_function docstring), each pixel p has an independent two-parameter block and the decoded value is

``GP[p] = −(sin(φ_2 + β_p) + sin(φ_1 + α_p)) / 2``

where φ_1 = arccos(1 − 2·I_1[p]/N) and φ_2 = arccos(1 − 2·I_2[p]/N) are the FRQI angles for the two channels (N is the normalisation used at encoding). Setting GP[p] = target[p] is solved by

``α_p = arcsin(−target[p]) − φ_1``
``β_p = arcsin(−target[p]) − φ_2``

giving the exact circuit output without any numerical optimisation.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default green ndarray

Matching-shape (2^n, 2^n) channel arrays. The argument names track the lab-historical (green, red) labels; the function is channel-agnostic and applies to any two intensity bands.

required red ndarray

required alpha float

Sensitivity correction factor for the second channel (the G-factor of the Generalized Polarization formula). Ignored when an explicit target is supplied.

None target ndarray | None

Optional explicit per-pixel target in [-1, 1]. When supplied, the solver fits the circuit to this target instead of the classical Generalized Polarization image. This is the entry point for the Corollary-1 extensions discussed in the companion paper: any bounded ratiometric operator of the two channels (Fura-2 calcium ratio, FRET efficiency, SNARF pH, NDVI, …) may be supplied as target and the closed form recovers the matching parameters.

docs.title: fold_gates
docs.text:
fold_gates(qc: QuantumCircuit, scale: float, *, target: Any | None = None) -> QuantumCircuit

Return qc with its gate noise amplified by global unitary folding.

The unitary part U (everything before the final measurements) is replaced by U (U^dag U)^k. For an odd integer scale this gives k = (scale - 1) / 2 full folds (1 -> U, 3 -> U U^dag U, ...). For other values the fractional remainder is realised by also folding the last m gates L of U once (... L^dag L), with m chosen so that the achieved scale 1 + 2k + 2m/d (d = number of gates in U) is as close as possible to the request. The achieved scale is stored in folded.metadata["zne_fold_scale"].

Final measurements (and the barriers just before them) are kept once, at the end. Barriers on the active qubits separate the copies, so a later optimisation pass cannot cancel U^dag U. Fold after transpilation to the device ISA, and pass the device target so the inverse gates (sxdg, rz(-t), ...) are rewritten into the basis without optimisation; the circuit layout is preserved.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default qc QuantumCircuit

Circuit to fold, ideally already transpiled to the device ISA. Measurements, if any, must all be final.

required scale float

Requested noise scale, >= 1. Odd integers give full folds.

required target Any | None

Optional transpiler Target. When given, gates outside its basis (introduced by the inverse) are translated into it.

None

For scale < 1, mid-circuit measurements, or other non-unitary operations (reset, control flow) in the unitary part.

docs.title: qimp.runtime.zne
docs.text:
Counts-side zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) helpers.

SamplerV2 exposes no ZNE option, so ZNE on bitstring distributions is done by hand in two steps:

  1. :func:fold_gates amplifies the gate noise of a circuit by global unitary folding, U -> U (U^dag U)^k, optionally with a partial fold of the last gates for fractional scales. Final measurements are kept at the end and never folded.
  2. :func:zne_extrapolate (or :func:zne_probabilities) fits each bitstring probability as a function of the noise scale and evaluates the fit at zero noise.

Folding is meant to be applied to a circuit that is already transpiled to the target ISA: the copies are separated by barriers and the inverse gates are rewritten into the target basis without optimisation, so nothing cancels U^dag U afterwards. Only gate noise is amplified; readout error is not scaled by folding and is left to TREX or another readout method.

docs.title: fold_gates
docs.text:
fold_gates(qc: QuantumCircuit, scale: float, *, target: Any | None = None) -> QuantumCircuit

Return qc with its gate noise amplified by global unitary folding.

The unitary part U (everything before the final measurements) is replaced by U (U^dag U)^k. For an odd integer scale this gives k = (scale - 1) / 2 full folds (1 -> U, 3 -> U U^dag U, ...). For other values the fractional remainder is realised by also folding the last m gates L of U once (... L^dag L), with m chosen so that the achieved scale 1 + 2k + 2m/d (d = number of gates in U) is as close as possible to the request. The achieved scale is stored in folded.metadata["zne_fold_scale"].

Final measurements (and the barriers just before them) are kept once, at the end. Barriers on the active qubits separate the copies, so a later optimisation pass cannot cancel U^dag U. Fold after transpilation to the device ISA, and pass the device target so the inverse gates (sxdg, rz(-t), ...) are rewritten into the basis without optimisation; the circuit layout is preserved.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default qc QuantumCircuit

Circuit to fold, ideally already transpiled to the device ISA. Measurements, if any, must all be final.

required scale float

Requested noise scale, >= 1. Odd integers give full folds.

required target Any | None

Optional transpiler Target. When given, gates outside its basis (introduced by the inverse) are translated into it.

None

Returns:

Type Description QuantumCircuit

The folded circuit, with the achieved scale in metadata["zne_fold_scale"].

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For scale < 1, mid-circuit measurements, or other non-unitary operations (reset, control flow) in the unitary part.

docs.title: zne_probabilities
docs.text:
zne_probabilities(counts_per_scale: Sequence[Mapping[str, float]], scales: Sequence[float], *, method: str = 'richardson') -> dict[str, float]

Extrapolate bitstring probabilities to zero noise.

Each counts_per_scale[i] is normalised to a probability distribution, and for every bitstring seen at any scale p(scale) is extrapolated to scale = 0. Negative estimates are clipped to zero and the result is renormalised to sum to one.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default counts_per_scale Sequence[Mapping[str, float]]

One counts (or probabilities) dict per noise scale.

required scales Sequence[float]

Noise scales matching counts_per_scale; at least two, distinct.

required method str

"richardson": polynomial of degree len(scales) - 1 through all points (exact for a quadratic trend with three scales). "linear": least-squares straight line. "exponential": p = 2^-n + B exp(-c scale), the decay of a global depolarising channel, with a linear fallback per bitstring.

'richardson'

Returns:

Type Description dict[str, float]

Zero-noise probabilities; bitstrings with zero estimate are dropped.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For an unknown method, mismatched lengths, fewer than two distinct scales, empty counts, or an all-zero estimate.

docs.title: zne_extrapolate
docs.text:
zne_extrapolate(counts_per_scale: Sequence[Mapping[str, float]], scales: Sequence[float], *, method: str = 'richardson', shots: int | None = None) -> dict[str, int]

Zero-noise extrapolated counts, in the same form as sampler counts.

Runs :func:zne_probabilities and rescales the result to integer counts with largest-remainder rounding, so the counts sum exactly to shots.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default counts_per_scale Sequence[Mapping[str, float]]

One counts dict per noise scale.

required scales Sequence[float]

Noise scales matching counts_per_scale.

required method str

Extrapolation model, one of ZNE_METHODS.

'richardson' shots int | None

Total of the returned counts. Defaults to the total count at the smallest scale.

None

Returns:

Type Description dict[str, int]

Extrapolated counts; zero-count bitstrings are dropped.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For non-positive shots or any error from :func:zne_probabilities.

docs.title: qimp.runtime.memory_pool

Pre-allocated buffer pool for batch image processing.

Avoids repeated np.zeros((H, W)) allocations when processing large datasets of same-shape images. Buffers are reused round-robin.

docs.title: MemoryPool
docs.text:
Round-robin pool of (H, W) image buffers and flattened angle buffers.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default max_buffers int

How many buffers to pre-allocate.

required image_size int

Side length of square buffers. Image buffer shape = (image_size, image_size), angle buffer shape = (image_size * image_size,).

required dtype type

Dtype of the buffers (default float32 — half the RAM of float64).

float32 Notes

No upper bound on image_size. With float32 and image_size=2^n × 2^n, one buffer costs 4 * 4^n bytes. A typical pool with 50 buffers at n=7 (128×128) uses ~3.2 MB; at n=10 (1024×1024) it uses ~200 MB.
